carry: All sorrow has one root: not knowing who I really am. Today, when something hurts, ask whose it is — the body's, the mind's, or mine?
ask: What would change today if I truly knew I am not this body?

carry: The path is not hidden — it is written here openly, for anyone who sincerely wants it. The only qualification is wanting it.
ask: Am I reading for information, or for my own transformation?

carry: One can be busy with rituals and miss the soul, or clever with ideas and miss it too. Watch today for both in yourself.
ask: Where am I doing without understanding, and where am I understanding without doing?

carry: A ritual done without inner change is a body without a soul. Pick one thing you do out of habit today and do it with full attention.
ask: Which of my practices have become automatic?

carry: Saying ‘it is all an illusion’ is easy; living free of delusion is the test. Let your conduct, not your words, show what you know.
ask: Where do my words run ahead of my life?

carry: Detachment and compassion bear fruit when they point toward the Self. Do one kind act today — and remember why you are doing it.
ask: Are my good deeds leading me inward, or just making me feel good?

carry: Without detachment there is no wisdom; but stopping at detachment and feeling satisfied is also a trap. Keep going.
ask: Have I grown comfortable with my spiritual progress?

carry: Wisdom is knowing what fits each moment. Today, before reacting, pause and ask what this situation truly calls for.
ask: Do I apply one rule to everything, or do I see what each moment needs?

carry: Real progress begins when you set your own opinions aside and listen. Try it today in one conversation — listen to understand.
ask: Which opinion of mine am I most unwilling to put down?

carry: A true Guru is known by Self-realisation, equanimity, actions free of desire, and words like no other. Notice what makes a presence uplifting.
ask: What qualities do I look for in the one I follow?

carry: The living Master's grace is nearest to us. Gratitude for a living guide awakens our own inner enquiry.
ask: Have I recognised how much I have received from those who guide me now?

carry: We cannot understand the divine by ourselves; it must be shown. Receive today's teaching as a gift, not a lesson.
ask: What has my Guru helped me see that I never could have seen alone?

carry: When the Guru is not physically near, the right scriptures hold us — if we are worthy of them. Read a few lines today with reverence.
ask: Do I read scripture to know more, or to become more?

carry: Return daily to what the Guru has asked you to study, leaving aside sectarian views. Consistency is its own teacher.
ask: What did my Guru ask me to reflect on that I have not yet returned to?

carry: Every soul that ever reached liberation stopped one thing: following its own will. Catch yourself today the moment you say ‘my way’.
ask: Where am I insisting on my own way?

carry: Self-will cannot see itself; it needs a living mirror. Other methods alone often make it stronger.
ask: Do I use my spiritual practice to feed my ego?

carry: Giving up self-will and stubborn views and living by the Guru's guidance is the seed of right faith itself.
ask: What would it feel like to follow guidance I don't fully understand yet?

carry: Pride and the passions are our greatest enemies, and they don't die by our own effort. In refuge, they fall away with little effort.
ask: Where has my pride quietly been in charge this week?

carry: Even after attaining omniscience, the disciple still bows to the Guru. Humility does not end with achievement.
ask: Do I stay humble after I succeed?

carry: Reverence is a path, not a formality. Only the fortunate understand why it matters so much.
ask: What does humility protect me from?

carry: Reverence is meant to free the disciple, never to serve the teacher. Respect every relationship where someone trusts you.
ask: Where have I been trusted — and have I honoured that trust?

carry: The same teaching lifts the sincere and misleads the stubborn. What we bring to the words decides what we take from them.
ask: Am I listening as a seeker or as someone defending a position?

carry: The signs of the stubborn mind are named without prejudice — so we can find them in ourselves, not in others.
ask: Can I read the next verses as a mirror rather than a magnifying glass?

carry: Outer renunciation alone, or a family tradition, does not make a true Guru. Look for inner realisation, not outward form.
ask: Do I follow anything only because it is familiar?

carry: The Jina is not the glowing body or the grand assembly; it is the pure, knowing soul. Look past appearances today.
ask: What do I admire in others — their outer glory or their inner state?

carry: Turning away from the living truth to follow what flatters us is pride in disguise. Notice when you seek praise in spiritual places.
ask: Do I seek where I am honoured, or where I am transformed?

carry: Knowing about heavens and holding to the right clothes is not knowledge that liberates. Ask what your learning is for.
ask: Which of my beliefs are really about identity, not truth?

carry: Taking vows without grasping their inner purpose only adds pride. Revisit one commitment today and remember why you made it.
ask: Do I take more pride in my practices than in my progress?

carry: Speaking of the pure Self while dropping all practice is losing the means. Keep both the vision and the effort.
ask: Have I used a lofty idea to excuse myself from effort?

carry: One with neither realisation nor practice drowns, and so do those who keep his company. Choose your influences with care.
ask: Whose company makes me more sincere, and whose makes me less?

carry: Both the ritualist and the dry intellectual can be driven by pride. When pride leads, truth recedes.
ask: How much of my spiritual life is quietly about being seen?

carry: Four things are missing in the stubborn: calm passions, inner detachment, simplicity, impartiality. Practise one of these today.
ask: Which of these four do I most lack?

carry: The faults are named to be removed, not judged. Now the Guru turns to the joy of the true seeker.
ask: Which one sign of the stubborn mind will I work on letting go of?

carry: Where there is Self-realisation, there is the true Guru. A true seeker looks for that, not for a family custom.
ask: Do I know why I trust those I trust?

carry: A true seeker treasures the living Guru and follows His word in thought, speech and deed. Let one action today be pure obedience.
ask: Are my mind, words and actions aligned in my devotion?

carry: There is only one path to the highest truth, in all three times. Honour whatever practice truly leads there.
ask: Do I judge practices by their label or by where they lead?

carry: A true seeker has one desire — the Self — and no other illness of the mind. Notice your other wants today without feeding them.
ask: If I could want only one thing, would it be this?

carry: Calm passions, a single longing for liberation, sorrow for endless births, compassion for all beings: where these live, the Self is near. Check your own heart against these four today.
ask: Which of these four is strongest in me, and which is weakest?

carry: Until we become worthy, even the best company and chances don't cure the inner illness. Prepare the ground.
ask: What is one thing I can do to become a more worthy receiver?

carry: When the seeker is ready, the Guru's words take root and right thinking blossoms, bringing real joy.
ask: When did a teaching suddenly make sense to me — and why then?

carry: Right thinking leads to Self-knowledge, and that dissolves delusion. Give ten quiet minutes today to thinking about who you are.
ask: What do I spend most of my thinking on?

carry: To awaken right thinking, the six truths are given as a dialogue between Guru and disciple. Bring your honest doubts.
ask: What is my sincerest doubt about the soul?

carry: The soul exists. It is eternal. It is the doer. It is the enjoyer. Liberation exists. The path exists. Say the six truths slowly today.
ask: Which of the six do I believe most easily, and which least?

carry: These six truths hold all six philosophies within them — given to make the highest truth understandable.
ask: Can I explain the six truths in my own words to someone else?

carry: The disciple's honest doubt: the soul can't be seen or touched, so how can it exist? Notice how much of you only trusts the senses.
ask: Do I believe only what I can see?

carry: Perhaps the soul is just the body, the senses, or the breath. The disciple dares to say what many quietly think.
ask: Do I live as if I am only this body?

carry: If the soul exists, why isn't it known like a pot or a cloth? A fair question — sit with it before rushing to the answer.
ask: What kind of things can be known without the senses?

carry: If there is no soul, the path is pointless. The disciple asks to be answered, not just told. Sincere doubt is welcome on this path.
ask: Do I bring my doubts to my Guru, or hide them?

carry: Soul and body seem one only because we have identified with the body for so long. Their signs are clearly different.
ask: When did I last feel distinct from my body — in prayer, in pain, in silence?

carry: Like a sword in its sheath, the soul lives in the body but is not the body. Picture the sword today when the body is tired or unwell.
ask: What changes when I see my body as a sheath?

carry: That which sees the seeing and knows every form — that unbroken awareness is the soul. Today, notice the one who is noticing.
ask: Who is aware of my thoughts right now?

carry: Each sense knows only its own world, but one knower holds all five together. That knower is you.
ask: What brings sight, sound and memory together into one experience?

carry: The body, senses and breath do not know the soul; they work because the soul is present. Feel the life behind your breath.
ask: What is the difference between a living body and a lifeless one?

carry: In waking, dreaming and deep sleep, something remains that knows them all. Consciousness is the sign that never fades.
ask: What in me has stayed the same through every stage of my life?

carry: You believe in the pot because you know it — yet doubt the knower? Knowledge itself proves the one who knows.
ask: Can there be knowing without a knower?

carry: A frail body can hold a brilliant mind, a large one a dull mind. If body and soul were one, this could not be.
ask: What does this tell me about where intelligence really lives?

carry: The living and the non-living have entirely separate natures, and they never become one, in any time.
ask: Where do I confuse what I am with what I have?

carry: The soul doubts the soul — what a wonder! The very doubter is the proof.
ask: Who is it in me that doubts?

carry: By reflecting within, the disciple is convinced: the soul exists. Real conviction comes from contemplation, not argument.
ask: What have I been convinced of only by argument, never by reflection?

carry: Now the next doubt: perhaps the soul is born with the body and dies with it. Notice how fear of death shapes your choices.
ask: Do I live as if death is the end?

carry: Everything changes moment to moment — so maybe the soul does too. Watch today how fast your moods shift, and who watches them.
ask: If everything about me changes, what is it that knows the changes?

carry: The body is a mix of matter — visible and lifeless. Who, then, could witness the soul's birth or death?
ask: Could I ever witness my own non-existence?

carry: To know something's birth and death, the knower must be separate from it. The witness of change is not the change.
ask: What in me witnesses change without changing?

carry: Of every combination we see, none produces consciousness. The soul is not made, so it is ever-present.
ask: Have I ever seen awareness come from something unaware?

carry: No one has ever seen consciousness arise from matter, or matter from consciousness. Rest in what experience tells you.
ask: What would I lose if I truly believed I am eternal? What would I gain?

carry: What is not made by any union cannot be destroyed by any separation. The soul is eternal.
ask: How would I treat today if I knew it was one of countless days?

carry: A snake's anger from birth speaks of tendencies carried from past lives. Our habits are older than we think.
ask: Which of my tendencies feel older than this lifetime?

carry: As a substance the soul is eternal; only its states change. The one who remembers childhood is still the same one now.
ask: Am I the same one who was a child? How do I know?

carry: One who knows and speaks of momentariness cannot himself be momentary. Look at your own experience.
ask: What in me has lasted through this whole day?

carry: No substance is ever completely destroyed. If the soul ended, what would it become?
ask: What changes in me when I see death as a change of state, not an ending?

carry: The disciple asks: maybe karma creates karma, or it just happens, or binding is simply our nature. Notice how often we say ‘it just happened’.
ask: Where do I avoid taking responsibility?

carry: Maybe the soul is untouched, and matter or God does it all. It is comforting to think we are not responsible.
ask: Whom or what do I blame for my situation?

carry: If the soul isn't the doer — or can never stop doing — then why seek liberation? A sharp question.
ask: Do I believe I can truly change?

carry: Matter cannot choose. If the conscious soul does not prompt karma, who does? Own your choices today.
ask: What did I do today that I would like to own fully?

carry: Karma binds only when the soul engages in craving and aversion. It is not automatic, and it is not our true nature — so it can end.
ask: Which craving or aversion bound me today?

carry: If the soul were already free, why don't you feel free? Purity is your nature, but it must be lived to be real.
ask: Where do I feel unfree right now, and what is holding me?

carry: God is the soul in its perfect, pure state — not one who pushes us to act. Our actions are our own.
ask: Do I relate to God as a judge, or as my own perfected nature?

carry: Abiding in its own nature, the soul is the doer of its purity. Forgetting it, the soul is the doer of karma. Stay aware today.
ask: In which moments today did I forget myself?

carry: Lifeless karma can't know when and how to give results — so how could the soul receive its fruits? The disciple keeps asking honestly.
ask: Do I believe my actions come back to me?

carry: If God gives the fruits of karma, God loses His godhood. Something about this idea doesn't fit.
ask: Do I expect someone else to reward or punish me?

carry: Without a ruling God, the disciple fears chaos and no place for results. Order doesn't need a ruler.
ask: What order do I see in my life that no one forces?

carry: Our feelings are conscious, and they draw karmic matter to us. Inner feelings are the real cause of bondage.
ask: What feeling did I nurture today without noticing?

carry: Poison and nectar don't know what they are, yet their effects are certain. So it is with good and bad karma. Choose what you consume — in food, in thought.
ask: What am I taking in that I will later have to digest?

carry: A pauper and a king: no effect without a cause. Differences in life are fruits of past karma.
ask: Can I meet my own circumstances without resentment?

carry: No one needs to hand out results — karma ripens by its own nature and then falls away.
ask: If this difficulty is old karma ripening, how can I let it pass peacefully?

carry: A deep subject, given briefly. Not everything must be understood at once; trust and keep reflecting.
ask: Which teaching do I keep for later, still unfolding?

carry: Infinite time has passed and the faults are still here — is liberation really possible? Feel the honesty of this doubt.
ask: Do I secretly believe I will never really change?

carry: Good karma, bad karma — the soul is never found without karma. Even heaven is not freedom.
ask: Am I seeking a better life, or a free one?

carry: As good and bad karma bear fruit, so does stopping them. Liberation is the fruit of ceasing. Stop one small harmful habit today.
ask: What could I simply stop doing?

carry: For infinite time we have lived in good and bad feelings. Cut them, and our true nature — freedom — shines.
ask: Can I watch a feeling today without being carried by it?

carry: Complete separation from body and karma, eternal rest in one's own infinite bliss: this is liberation.
ask: When have I tasted even a little of joy that needed nothing outside me?

carry: How can karma from endless time be cleared in one short life? Remember: darkness of a thousand years leaves in a moment of light.
ask: Do I underestimate what one lifetime can do?

carry: So many faiths, so many paths — which one is true? Look for what all true paths share.
ask: What do the wisest people I know have in common?

carry: Which caste, which clothes lead to liberation? The disciple is confused by divisions. Notice labels that divide.
ask: Which labels do I put on myself and others?

carry: If there is no clear path, what use is knowing about the soul? Even despair is honest when spoken to the Guru.
ask: What would make all this worthwhile for me?

carry: ‘Five answers have satisfied me; if I knew the path too, how fortunate I would be!’ Feel the disciple's longing.
ask: How strong is my longing, really?

carry: As you were convinced by the five answers, the path too will become clear naturally. Trust the process.
ask: Where have I already received clarity I once doubted I would find?

carry: Karma is ignorance; liberation is abiding in the Self. As light ends darkness, knowing ends ignorance.
ask: What would one moment of real Self-awareness look like for me today?

carry: Whatever binds is the path of bondage; whatever cuts it is the path of liberation. Simple and complete.
ask: What in my day today was binding me, and what was freeing me?

carry: Attachment, aversion and ignorance are the main knots. Whatever loosens them is the path. Loosen one knot today.
ask: Which knot is tightest in me — attachment, aversion, or ignorance?

carry: The soul is existence and consciousness, free of illusion. Whatever brings you to experience it is the path.
ask: What brings me closest to inner stillness?

carry: Of all karma, deluding karma is the chief. Destroy it, and the rest follows.
ask: What delusion do I cling to most?

carry: Delusion of belief falls to enlightenment; delusion of conduct falls to dispassion. This remedy never fails.
ask: Is my struggle more with seeing clearly, or with living what I see?

carry: Anger binds; forgiveness frees. Everyone has felt this. Forgive one person today, even silently.
ask: Whom do I need to forgive?

carry: Drop insistence on your own view and walk the path, and liberation is only a few births away.
ask: Which of my views am I most attached to?

carry: You asked six questions thoughtfully. Understand all six truths fully, from every side — that is the sure path.
ask: Which of the six truths do I need to study more deeply?

carry: There is no caste or clothing on this path. Whoever walks it, arrives.
ask: Do I see every soul as equally capable of liberation?

carry: Calm passions, one longing, sorrow for endless births, compassion within — these mark the true aspirant. Check these four again today.
ask: Has any of these four grown in me since I last looked?

carry: When such an aspirant meets the Guru's teaching, faith awakens and the inner search begins.
ask: What is the next step in my inner search?

carry: Dropping fixed views and following the Guru, one experiences the pure Self — the same for every seeker, without division.
ask: What would it mean to have experience rather than opinion?

carry: Direct experience, steady attention, firm conviction, and attention flowing inward — this is the highest right faith.
ask: Where does my attention flow when I have nothing to do?

carry: As right faith grows, delusion falls away, and conduct rises into complete dispassion.
ask: How has my conduct changed as my understanding grew?

carry: Unbroken absorption in one's own nature is omniscience — liberation, even while in the body.
ask: What would unbroken peace feel like?

carry: A dream of millions of years ends the moment you wake. So too, endless delusion ends with knowing. Waking can happen at any moment.
ask: What would ‘waking up’ mean in my life today?

carry: Let go of identifying with the body, and you are no longer the doer or the enjoyer of karma. This is the heart of religion.
ask: Can I do my work today without the feeling of ‘I am doing it’?

carry: By this religion alone is liberation — and you yourself are liberation, infinite knowing, unobstructed. Remember this when you feel small.
ask: What would I do today if I believed I am already whole?

carry: Pure, awake, full of consciousness, self-luminous, the home of bliss — what more to say? Reflect, and you will reach it.
ask: When did I last sit quietly simply to reflect on who I am?

carry: All the Enlightened Ones agree, and it is all here. Having said it, the Guru falls silent in natural absorption. Give silence a place today.
ask: Can I spend five minutes in silence without filling it?

carry: Through the Guru's teaching came an awareness never known before; the Self was found within, and ignorance was gone.
ask: What has my Guru's teaching awakened in me?

carry: I am pure consciousness — ageless, deathless, indestructible, beyond the body. Say it to yourself once today and feel it.
ask: What would ageing mean if I were truly beyond the body?

carry: The soul does and endures karma only while in delusion. When attention flowed into the Self, the doer disappeared.
ask: When does the feeling of ‘doing’ fall away for me?

carry: Or say: I now do and enjoy only my own pure states, free of thought. Real joy has no object.
ask: What pure state can I rest in today?

carry: Liberation is the purity of one's own Self; whatever reaches it is the path. The whole path is here in brief.
ask: Can I state the whole path in one sentence?

carry: Aho! Aho! O Sadguru, boundless ocean of compassion — what grace on this unworthy one! Let gratitude fill one moment today.
ask: What am I most grateful to my Guru for?

carry: What can I offer at Your feet? Everything is less than the soul, and You gave me the soul. I can only live at Your command.
ask: What can I offer today?

carry: From today, may this body and all be at the Lord's service. I am a servant, a servant, the humblest servant.
ask: How can I serve today with no thought of reward?

carry: By explaining the six truths, You showed me separate from the body, like a sword from its sheath. Your grace is beyond measure.
ask: Do I still feel the sword and the sheath as separate?

carry: All six philosophies are contained in these six truths. Reflect on them deeply, and no doubt remains.
ask: Which doubt still lingers for me?

carry: No illness like self-delusion; the Sadguru is the expert physician, His word the regimen, contemplation the medicine. Take your medicine today.
ask: Am I following the regimen, or only admiring the doctor?

carry: If you want the highest, make real effort — don't hide behind ‘fate’ or ‘it's not my time’.
ask: What excuse do I use most often?

carry: Hearing about the pure Self, don't drop your practice. Keep the absolute in view and keep doing the work.
ask: Is my practice steady, or has understanding made me lazy?

carry: Neither the absolute view alone nor the practical view alone — both together. Balance is the teaching.
ask: Do I lean too far toward theory or toward practice?

carry: Sectarian ideas are not right practice; and the absolute view without awareness of the Self is empty.
ask: Is my practice alive with awareness?

carry: The Enlightened of past, present and future all walk the same path. There is no difference in the way.
ask: Can I see the same truth in teachers of different traditions?

carry: Every soul is like the Siddha by nature; whoever understands this becomes it. The Guru's word and the Jina's state are the helpers.
ask: Can I see the Siddha in the person I find hardest to love?

carry: Using ‘the soul is everything’ as an excuse to drop the Guru and the help — that keeps one in delusion. Value the support you are given.
ask: Do I undervalue the support I have been given?

carry: Talking wisdom while delusion lives within betrays the Enlightened Ones. Let your inner life match your words.
ask: Is there something I preach that I don't yet practise?

carry: Compassion, peace, equanimity, forgiveness, truth, renunciation, detachment — ever awake in the seeker's heart. Live one of the seven fully today.
ask: Which of the seven is most awake in me today?

carry: Where delusion is destroyed or calmed, that is the state of the wise; all else is illusion.
ask: Where has my delusion calmed a little this year?

carry: To the Enlightened, the whole world is like leftover food, or a dream. Otherwise it is only talk.
ask: What worldly thing still pulls at me most?

carry: Reflect on the first five truths, live the sixth, and you will reach the fifth — liberation. No doubt about it.
ask: What will I do today to live the sixth truth?

carry: Countless salutations at the feet of that Enlightened One who, though in a body, lives beyond it. Bow today, inwardly, to your Guru.
ask: How do I want to carry this verse into tomorrow?
